title: Encrypted DNS Discovery RFC 9463 DHCPv4 OPTION_V4_DNR Wire Architecture
purpose: Define the RFC 9463 DHCPv4 OPTION_V4_DNR wire-format boundary for encrypted DNS discovery data.
design_summary: The DHCPv4 slice adds a pure OPTION_V4_DNR codec that writes and parses the RFC 9463 option tag, one-octet length, repeated DNR Instance Data entries, service-priority, RFC 8415 DNS-name, IPv4 address-length/address list, RFC 9460 SvcParams, ADN-only mode, Parameter Request List value, RFC 3396 concatenated option segments, service-priority sorting, and invalid-instance discard behavior.
data_and_state_considerations: The helper owns only DHCPv4 option bytes and normalized instance values. It does not own DHCP client state, lease handling, platform resolver installation, certificate validation, DHCPv6, or Neighbor Discovery encoding.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Single OPTION_V4_DNR encoding is rejected when option data exceeds 255 octets.
RFC 3396 segment encoding splits oversized option data across repeated OPTION_V4_DNR TLVs.
ADN-only instances omit Addr Length, IPv4 addresses, and SvcParams.
Populated instances require non-zero Addr Length that is a multiple of 4.
IPv4 loopback and multicast addresses are discarded during decode, and an instance with no usable address is invalid.
Multiple DNR Instance Data entries remain separate and are returned in service-priority order.
risks: This slice does not implement Neighbor Discovery encrypted DNS option padding or lifetime processing.
This slice does not implement a DHCPv4 client, lease state, or platform resolver configuration.
This slice does not implement PKIX validation or encrypted resolver connection establishment.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The codec sits beside the DHCPv6 OPTION_V6_DNR helper and below any platform DHCP client integration. It gives ProtocolLab and future network adapters exact DHCPv4 byte-level proof without moving DHCP state into the QUIC runtime.
